items.title: Aetna Says It Doesn't Use Repricing Tools In Antitrust Case - Law360
items.reason: This item reports an antitrust litigation development involving a major payer (Aetna) making substantive claims about its business practices in a legal proceeding, which directly falls under payer litigation enforcement.
items.summary: Aetna has asserted in an antitrust case that it does not use repricing tools, likely in response to allegations or discovery related to how it processes and adjusts claim payments. Repricing tools are mechanisms used to alter provider reimbursement rates, and Aetna's denial of their use suggests the plaintiff is challenging the payer's claims-processing and payment methodologies as potentially anticompetitive. This litigation is relevant to revenue-cycle teams because repricing and claims-adjustment practices directly impact provider reimbursement and network economics, and any ruling could establish precedent on what payer tools and practices are permissible under antitrust law.
